title: Frontiers: The Impact of Loosening Concealed Carry Laws on Firearm Demand
eligible_reason: Design qualifies: two separately analyzed binary state-law treatments (CCW Shall Issue adoption: treated DC, IA, WI, IL vs. 8 never-treated control states; CCW Permitless Carry adoption: 9 treated states vs. 24 never-treated controls), each with multiple adoption dates over 2010-2017, estimated with Callaway-Sant'Anna on state-month and county-month panels. However, every main-text specification is a conditional CSA whose covariates are time-varying (Stand Your Ground indicator, lagged gun deaths per 100K, Democratic vote share in nearest presidential election; BGC models add Point-of-Contact status; mortality models use lagged total BGCs, lagged unemployment, alcohol consumption), so no main-text spec satisfies the no-time-varying-controls rule. n_eligible_specs = 0; borderline case for lead review. REPLICATION CHECK (Nov 1, 2026, from package code and data): confirmed. Every att_gt call is preceded by covariate adjustment (table3.R/table5.R/figure2.R residualize the outcome on covariates x (t-g+1); table4.R passes xformla). lag_total_gundeaths_percap has ~33 distinct values per state (monthly) and democrats 3 (by election); Table 5 uses monthly lagged BGCs, monthly lagged unemployment and yearly alcohol consumption. syg, poc and poc_partial are time-invariant in-sample but never appear without a time-varying covariate. No specification uses only time-invariant covariates or none. Paper set to eligible = false; specs moved to ineligible_specs.
design_notes: Panels: state-month (online purchases and NICS background checks) and county-month (online purchases) 2010-2017. Treatment split into two conditions (Table 1); six states adopting SYG near CCW changes are dropped (MO, AK, VT, NV, NC, PA). CS estimator with covariates, untreated potential outcome Y_it(0) = theta_t + eta_i + X_it' beta_t + v_it (beta_t restricted to beta in state-month models, footnote 3); never-treated controls; observations weighted by state/county population; SE bootstrapped clustered by state. Reported summary = '1-year ATT' (average of 12 post-adoption monthly ATTs) in Tables 3-5 and event-study plots by event time in Figure 2 (state-month, Shall Issue; -12 to +12 months). Covariates vary over time (lagged gun deaths monthly, SYG adoption, vote share by election), so specs are recorded as ineligible_with_controls. Robustness with alternative specifications in Web Appendix B.2 and D.1 only.
estimators_reported: Callaway-Sant'Anna (conditional, never-treated controls, population weights, state-clustered bootstrap)
software: R (did 2.1.2, tidyverse, lfe loaded but unused)
replication_feasible: no (ineligible; also online-purchase and mortality outcomes are synthetic in the package, only NICS background-check outcomes are original)
screener_notes: Package not in our set; the article states 'The web appendix and data files are available at https://doi.org/10.1287/mksc.2023.0480' (INFORMS supplement). Online firearm transaction data come from a proprietary online retail platform (representativeness acknowledged); NICS background checks, CDC mortality, RAND law dates are public. Every main-text estimate is a conditional CSA with time-varying covariates (SYG, lagged gun deaths, Dem vote share; POC for BGCs; lagged BGCs/unemployment/alcohol for mortality). Unconditional CSA/TWFE versions are not reported in the main text (alternative specifications in Web Appendix B.2/D.1). If the lead treats base-period covariates in the did package as admissible, or accepts an unconditional re-estimation as a deviation, this paper has 12 state-month plus 10 county-month static specs and a 6-panel event study (Shall Issue) with never-treated controls and population weights. REPLICATION AGENT: package found at ~/did_packages/mksc/mksc.2023.0480/replication/ (R code + state.csv/county.csv). Authors' table3.R re-run reproduces the six BGC point estimates exactly (original data); online-purchase columns do not reproduce (synthetic data). Unconditional candidate specs for the six BGC columns were run and parked in ~/did_packages/_work/mksc.2023.0480/candidate_specs/ (not in data/specs/).
